reading: Every row is: left colour, then a run of the middle colour, then (maybe) a third colour. Each middle run slides left until its right end sits on the shape's leftmost right edge (col 5 in both pairs), but never past col 0; the left colour fills the cells it leaves. The third colour is untouched.

slots.subject: the middle-colour run in each row (the shape between the left colour and the third colour)
slots.target column: min over rows of the run's right end
slots.fill: the row's left colour fills the cells the run leaves
slots.clamp: the run's start stays >= 0 (rows that are too long end past the target column)

why: in every row the run keeps its length and ends at the target column, or starts at col 0 if it is too long
invariants: run length and colour count per row

reading: One object has a one-cell-wide stalk reaching to the other object. Its body slides along the stalk until it touches the other object, and the stalk disappears.

new_rows.name: stalk
new_rows.datalog:
stalk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Ya = Y - 1, Yb = Y + 1, !px(Ya, X, C), !px(Yb, X, C).
stalk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Xa = X - 1, Xb = X + 1, !px(Y, Xa, C), !px(Y, Xb, C).

new_rows.name: body
new_rows.datalog:
stalk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Ya = Y - 1, Yb = Y + 1, !px(Ya, X, C), !px(Yb, X, C).
stalk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Xa = X - 1, Xb = X + 1, !px(Y, Xa, C), !px(Y, Xb, C).
stalked(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), stalk(Y, X).
body(Y, X) :- stalked(O), obj(O, Y, X), !stalk(Y, X).

why: the body keeps its shape and ends touching the other object; any stalk cells left over become background (0)

reading: Columns of 0 cut the input into three 4x4 panels of 5. Each panel's hole pattern names a colour, and output row i is filled with panel i's colour: no hole is 2, a centre 2x2 hole is 8, a bottom-centre hole is 4, side holes are 3.

slots.panels: the three 4x4 panels between the 0 separator columns
slots.key: hole pattern -> colour: none->2, centre->8, bottom-middle->4, left+right edges->3
slots.output: 3x3 grid, row i is all key(panel i)

why: each output row is one colour, set by the pattern of the matching panel
invariants: panel order left to right equals row order top to bottom

reading: Each single cell draws a line in its own colour right to the grid edge, then down the last column until the row just above the next line (or the bottom edge).

new_rows.name: rend
new_rows.datalog:
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rend(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), wmax(X).

why: the horizontal part reaches the right edge; the vertical part runs down the last column and stops at the first cell that is not background (the next line's end) or at the bottom edge

reading: A frame has four sides in four colours (corners empty), and an 8-shape the size of its interior sits elsewhere. The output is the frame box with the 8-shape placed inside. Each 8 cell takes the colour of its nearest side, and stays 8 when two sides tie.

slots.container: the box of the four-sided frame (sides kept, corners 0)
slots.content: the 8-coloured shape, whose box equals the frame interior
slots.tint: each 8 cell -> colour of the nearest side; ties stay 8; 0 stays 0

why: output = frame box; interior = 8-shape recoloured by nearest side

reading: Count each colour. The output has one column per colour, ordered by count from most to least. Each column is filled from the top with that colour for count cells; the rest is 0. Height = the largest count.

slots.colours: the distinct colours of the input
slots.bar: column j = colour j repeated count(j) times from the top, then 0
slots.size: height = max count, width = number of colours

why: each output column is a top-aligned bar whose length equals that colour's input count

reading: The grid is split into an 8 area and a 1 area. Each 2-object slides sideways inside its area: left in the 8 area, right in the 1 area, until it reaches the edge of the area or the grid.

slots.areas: the two big background areas (colour 8 and colour 1)
slots.subject: each 2-object
slots.stop: the area boundary or the grid border

why: each 2-object keeps its shape and row span and ends flush with its area's left (8) or right (1) edge

reading: Two big coloured areas each hold rectangular blobs of an inner colour. Each one-cell defect on a blob's rectangle (a one-cell bump outside it or a one-cell dent inside it) becomes a 2-cell line across the rectangle edge, in the other big area's colour.

slots.areas: the two large areas (e.g. 8 and 4; 4 and 2; 3 and 2)
slots.blobs: the near-rectangular inner-colour shapes in each area
slots.defects: single cells where the blob deviates from its rectangle: bumps outside or dents inside
slots.mark: defect cell + the next cell across the rectangle edge, perpendicular to it, painted in the other area's colour

why: every bump or dent becomes a 2-cell line crossing the rectangle boundary; nothing else changes

reading: In each row, the run of 3s at the right slides left until it hits an 8 or the left edge. Rows move independently, and 8s stay put.

slots.subject: each horizontal run of 3 in a row (rows move separately, so a vertical stack of 3s splits)
slots.stop: the first 8 to the left, or the grid edge

why: each row's 3-run keeps its length and ends next to the nearest 8 on its left, or at column 0

reading: In a 5/0 noise grid, each cluster of 2s lies in a 3x3 window that has no 0 and a 5 at its centre. Inside that window the centre becomes 4, the other 5s become 7, and the 2s stay. Windows do not overlap, and each one covers its whole cluster.

slots.windows: 3x3 blocks with no 0 and centre 5 that hold a whole 2-cluster (non-overlapping)
slots.paint: centre -> 4, other 5 cells in window -> 7, 2 cells kept

why: every change lies in one such window; the window holds 0 zeros; 2s never change
